content.text:
I submitted **index 26** (Mg 0.24 / Sb 0.76) as the best composition. It had the highest EQE I measured, but that value is only 0.00106%, so everything in this Mg–Sb oxide library performed poorly.

I used all 3 EQE measurements and 2 of the 5 XRD scans:

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | 0.38 | −0.00006 (effectively zero) |
| 23 | 0.67 | 0.00043 |
| 26 | 0.76 | 0.00106 |

- **Why the Sb-rich end:** the band-gap model predicts about 1.2 eV for an Sb-rich phase (MgSb4O10), which would absorb the 2.7 eV light. MgSb2O6 is predicted at 2.82 eV, just above the photon energy. The Mg-rich phases are predicted at 3.1 eV and 4.2 eV, too wide to absorb it.
- **XRD:** index 26 shows extra peaks that index 23 lacks, which points to a second phase. However, the measured patterns matched none of the database phases well (best similarity 0.20), so I can't say which phases are actually present.
- **Mg-rich side:** I didn't measure it. The stability model puts Mg3SbO4 far above the stable hull, so those films are probably MgO plus the 4.2 eV-gap Mg4Sb2O9. The near-zero result at index 13 fits that.

Index 26 is the Sb-rich edge of the library, and EQE rose toward it with every measurement. If the true peak lies anywhere, it is most likely at or near index 26.
